top_story_title: KEV-listed Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 reaches both Cisco and Palo Alto Networks portfolios
top_story_summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 with a remediation due date of 2026-11-10. The KEV entry describes an unchecked return value in Google Brotli that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt adjacent decoder state memory using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream, with possible outcomes of memory disclosure, denial of service or arbitrary code execution. Brotli is a compression library, not a device, which is why this lands as a portfolio problem rather than a single advisory.
top_actions: Open the Cisco advisory (cisco-sa-oct2026-node-js-Jj3SQ19u) and the Palo Alto Networks page for CVE-2026-111497, and extract the affected-product and fixed-release tables - do not assume a build number, check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
Cross-match those product lists against your asset inventory by model and running version; record patched / mitigated / accepted risk per device group in the change record.
Treat CVE-2026-111497 as KEV with a due date of 2026-11-10: schedule internet-facing and federal-scope devices first, HA pair secondary before primary.

Because CVE-2026-105483 and CVE-2026-106069 are TLS hostname validation bypasses, review which outbound TLS sessions your devices initiate (cloud management, telemetry, licensing, update servers) and pin or egress-filter those destinations until patched.
Remove management access (HTTPS/SSH/API) from untrusted and internet-facing interfaces on the affected platforms, and restrict it to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
executive_summary: CVE-2026-111497, the KEV-listed Brotli decoder flaw, hit both Cisco (bundled with three Node.js DNS/TLS bugs, SIR High) and Palo Alto Networks (portfolio status, CRITICAL) on the same day; CISA's due date for it was 2026-11-10.
Barracuda says attackers are now exploiting two recently patched Email Security Gateway flaws to execute commands as root - confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of an edge appliance.
Cisco shipped a Meraki OS hardening release covering multiple internally found vulnerabilities, with no workarounds and no known exploitation.
Palo Alto Networks disclosed CVE-2026-0250, a medium-severity buffer overflow in the GlobalProtect app triggered when connecting to a portal or gateway.

N-able pulled hosted N-central offline and told on-premises customers to shut servers down after 33 zero-days with PoC exploits were published - not network gear, but it holds privileged access into managed estates.
No network vendor described a defensive AI capability in this window, and nothing in the items is genuinely AI-related.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Read the affected-product list in the Cisco advisory and filter your inventory by model and running version; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release rather than assuming a build.
**Cisco** — Prioritise internet-facing and federal-scope devices against the KEV due date of 2026-11-10, then schedule the rest inside the normal change window, HA secondary first.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Open the portfolio status page for CVE-2026-111497, note which products and versions are listed as affected, and check the vendor advisory for the fixed release - no version number should be assumed.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Confirm running versions across your estate against that table; schedule the upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first.

**Barracuda** — Verify that every ESG appliance actually has the recent patches applied - exploitation is of already-patched flaws, so unpatched units are the live exposure; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.

**Barracuda** — Treat root-capable command execution as potential compromise: rotate appliance admin credentials, API tokens, certificates and any directory or mail service accounts configured on the ESG.
**Cisco** — Identify your Meraki estate by model and current firmware in the dashboard, and compare against the fixed versions named in the advisory.

**Cisco** — Because no workarounds exist, schedule the hardening release through the dashboard firmware management: controllers and security appliances first, then a staged access point and switch rollout.

headlines.title: Hackers now exploit critical Barracuda ESG flaws to gain root access
headlines.summary: Attackers are exploiting two recently patched Barracuda Email Security Gateway flaws to run commands with root privileges, the vendor warned.

headlines.title: N-able Takes N-central Cloud Offline After Researcher Discloses 33 Zero-Days with PoC Exploits
